description.purpose: The one way to operate models in a colony (GH #855): a catalogue of model PACKAGES, the replacements an operator sets, the tier index, and the hand that resolves every subscribed brain by one precedence and pushes the package in. Four cells, no clock, and no model in any resolution. `store` holds one package per model (id, endpoint, wire dialect, the per-model parameters in `package`, the per-model prompt block in `prompt`, cent-integer prices -- a store column has no float), `tiers`, `overrides` (global: model X everywhere -> Y; targeted: a path prefix -> Y), `subscribers` with their start value and what they resolved to, a `resolutions` journal of every lookup and every push, and `incidents` as a plain field log. `select` turns requirements into ONE resolution by comparison and refuses rather than guesses. `hand` is deterministic code: targeted > global > prose > tier > start value, a package pushed as a params-only message with `$reset` for every key it does not set, and only when the package changed -- the healing path must never run through the model that broke. 2.2.1 repairs the two doors: they clear the context keys of the internal store round trip (`lr_phase`, `lr_carry`, `registry_origin`), so a message from outside cannot pose as a store answer -- and since 2.3.0 as a translation either. Since 2.3.0 (GH #858) a cell may state in PROSE what it needs (the llm param `requirement`); `translate`, the one llm cell in here, chooses a model from the catalogue for it once per (requirement, catalogue) pair, `hand` checks the choice against the catalogue and stores it with its reason in `translations`, and every resolution after that is a read of that row. The catalogue ships a handful of rows a hosted provider lists publicly (prices and context as of 2026-09-26), and the operator keeps it on `in_hand` with `model_upsert` and `model_retire`. Since 2.3.1 (GH #863) a push the addressed cell refuses comes back on the road it came by to a third door, `in_refused`: the hand marks the subscriber row `refused` with the cell's own reason when the refused model is the one it holds, `show` names it until the next push or a `reset`, and a `reset` sends a refused package again. The three page bounds of 2.1.0 and the new `catalog_rows` are PARAMS of the cells that read them ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138), ruling R-0904-6); what is left in `.env` for this template is nothing. Since 2.3.2 ([#886](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/886)) `./translate` declares `hop.model`, the model that answered its translation; nothing else moved. Since 2.4.0 ([#890](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/890)) a model row carries `cache_mode` and `cache_ttl_s`, `./hand` pushes both with `context_window` in the package, and `./translate` declares every hop key the `llm` cell writes. A package can now say how its provider caches, so it is the second digit. Since 2.5.0 ([#957](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/957)) a row whose `wire_dialect` is `decisions` is a typed decisions model, served only to a subscriber that states `"protocol": "decisions"`; every resolution skips a row of the other protocol, a decisions subscriber may start on no model, and the catalogue carries one decisions row. A subscriber can say what it could not before, so it is the second digit. Since 2.5.1 ([#965](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/965)) the catalogue's decisions row names no endpoint, so a push leaves a decider on the base URL its set gives it. Only a seed row moved, so it is the third digit. Since 2.6.0 ([#993](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/993)) a catalogue row's `package` may carry `supported_params`, pushed with the model like every package key, and `./translate` declares `hop.dropped`. A subscriber can rely on what was never promised before, so it is the second digit.
description.use_when: Once per colony, as a sibling of the agents -- `meclaw-os` instantiates it as `/os/llm-registry` since 1.9.0. The division of labour is the point: a cell is BORN on its start value (`${ctx.model}`, `${MODEL_*}` at boot), and this hive is the living record of what it runs now and why. A cell whose template states a `requirement` is served by its translation; one without keeps the tier or start value it had in 2.2.0. Set a replacement or move a tier on `in_hand` when a model has to change under running cells; read `show` to see, per cell, the model, the rank that chose it, the reason and since when.
description.not_in_scope: No control loop: no probe, no timer, no incident rule -- an `incidents` row changes nothing by itself, and the absence of automation is pinned by a test (GH #130 holds the target picture). No model in the resolution: the translator answers a question at most once per change and its own model is a start value the registry never resolves, so a failing translator leaves every cell on the resolution it had. Four honest limits ride along: the registry must PUSH because a cell cannot read the colony (eventual consistency, running calls finish on the old model, and the registry knows what it sent and, since 2.3.1, what came back refused -- never what a cell runs); a subscriber needs a road -- in `meclaw-os` the builder draws it with the generation, elsewhere somebody does; `provider`, `api_key` and the auth dimension are immutable per cell and `base_url` moves only inside the cell's `base_url_allow`, so the package is the boundary and a model behind another credential is a rebirth; and token spend lives in the message log, not here.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty since GH #228; an edge naming ./select, ./hand or ./store is refused with hive_port_boundary), and what a caller wants rides on hop.route. in_select: the request as a tool_call turn ({tier?, capability?, max_cost?, min_context?}), promoting the asker to context.asker. answer: a lookup's result (hop.resolved / hop.reason_code / hop.model_id) or the view `show` returns. in_hand: a command (since 2.3.0 also `model_upsert`, `model_retire`, `retranslate`), or an announcement of brains from the tree in context.model_announced, promoting the deciding identity to context.actor -- a command with no actor is REFUSED. ack: accepted or rejected plus a reason_code and the counts. update: hop.route=='update' && hop.subscriber=='<cell path>', hop.rank naming the rule -- one edge per subscriber into the composite's `in_model` door. error: into a drain the parent MUST wire. `incidents` has NO writer among these lanes: a parent's params.graph edge straight into ./store maintains it (and may still write `models`), which the hive port seal does not touch because the bootstrap is deliberately outside its scope. `models` (since 2.3.0, `model_upsert` / `model_retire`), `tiers`, `overrides`, `subscribers`, `translations` and `resolutions` are written by the two code cells in here. contract.write_surface 'internal' refuses a transfer import from outside the hive.
{"tier":"mid"} -> the model the index points at, with provider, wire dialect, window and cent price, reason_code tier_active, and one resolutions line

{"capability":["tools","vision"],"max_cost":500} -> the cheapest active model that has both; rank cost_out asc, cost_in asc, context_window desc, model_id asc -- total, so the same request resolves the same way forever
{"max_cost":1} -> resolved:false, model_id "", reason_code no_candidate -- no nearest match, no default, and the refusal is journalled

{"op":"remap","tier":"mid","model_id":"provider-b/model-large"} -> the tier row supersedes and every UNPINNED mid subscriber whose package changed gets one params-only message it answers with silence: no inference, no provider call, no cost
a pinned subscriber row is a decision written down -- the remap does not reach it, and one journal line says it was skipped, so a query shows which cells a remap misses

{"op":"override_set","scope":"global","match":"provider-a/model-mid","model_id":"provider-b/model-large"} -> every unpinned subscriber whose tier or start value is provider-a/model-mid moves; the push is the whole package of provider-b/model-large (model, endpoint, dialect, `package`, `prompt` as model_prompt) plus `$reset` for every package key it does not set

{"op":"override_set","scope":"target","match":"/os/orgs/acme/members/alex/assistants/scribe/talky/brain","model_id":"provider-b/model-large"} -> exactly that brain moves, pinned or not; `override_clear` with the id the ack returned puts it back on what it resolves to without it, and falling back to the start value is a push of `$reset` alone

{"op":"show"} -> one entry per subscriber on `answer`: cell_path, model_id, rank (target | global | prose | tier | start), reason, the translator's sentence as `because` when the rank is prose, requirement, since, pinned

{"op":"subscribe","cell_path":"/os/argus/judge","start_model":"<start>","requirement":"Judges proposed changes to the colony; careful reasoning over speed and price."} -> one question to ./translate (none if this requirement is already answered for this catalogue), one row in `translations`, one push ranked prose

{"op":"model_retire","model_id":"<id>"} -> the row goes `retired` (never a result again), every subscriber is resolved again, and each distinct requirement the new catalogue has not answered is asked once; until an answer is a row, the last translation whose model is still active holds
